newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey plans to issue gold investment certificates.
newsitem.headline: Turkey plans to issue gold investment certificates.

text.p: Turkey plans to issue gold investment certificates to attract part of the estimated 6,000 tonnes of gold held by Turkish citizens under a revenue-raising package, a senior gold official said on Monday.

"Our studies showed that the gold in Turkish citizens' hands was worth at least 6,000 tonnes...and we want to transfer 10-15 percent of it to the economic process," Kaan Rasim Aytogu, sectretary general of Istanbul's Gold Bourse and chief adviser to Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, told Reuters.
Aytogu said the gold certificates would carry eight to nine percent annual interest.
The government plans to convert the gold into bullion through Turkey's first gold refinery, which is set to begin operations by the beginning of 1998.
Aytogu is to fly to Australia on Tuesday to sign with representatives of Australia's Gold Corporation an accord on establishing the gold refinery.
"Turkey must have bullion gold circulated in the international markets," Ismail Yanik, chairman of the Istanbul Gold Bourse Members Association, told Reuters.
Aytogu said work was progressing on a project to make Turkey the centre of a new area for world gold trade in 10 years.

"South Africa gold prices are increasing because of high costs, and the importance of the existing South Africa-Europe gold trade arc is fading," he said, adding, "The new arc will begin from Australia-Papua New Guinea-Indonesia and jump to Central Asian producers Kazakhstan-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan and they need another point to access consumers in the Middle East and North Africa."
He said the strongest candidate for this role was Turkey, a leading consumer with 10 percent of annual world supply.
